The Community Discords Program is an initiative announced by Blizzard Entertainment on 8 June 2023 to formalize collaboration with independently run Discord servers dedicated to World of Warcraft in Europe. The program establishes guidelines for participation and outlines the benefits available to approved servers. The program's stated aim is to strengthen community engagement and provide structured support for player-driven initiatives. It reflects Blizzard’s broader approach to integrating official communication with community platforms. Comprehend Scroll is a mage ability used to translate undeciphered scrolls into usable items. The mage's Comprehension skill starts at 1, and is increased by 1 for every scroll successfully deciphered. This is the version of Comprehension Charm items from . It is possible for this spell to backfire, polymorphing the mage into a sheep for 8 seconds. The scroll is not consumed if this occurs.

Rufinwag nicknamed Cooktholomew is a chef from Booty Bay. He had been traveling with Bonenose and a pair of Booty Bay Buccaneers, but got lost at sea. The group wouldn't continue without their meal, so Bonenose sent the hero to Booty Bay to help prepare the meal. He was good friends with Kelsey Yance and Scowling Rosa, and would bunk with the other chefs of the city in an area managed by Mrs. Gant. Cooktholomew had hidden his notes on the recipe in the Property of Cooktholomew.

Cooking Impossible is a PvP Brawl where two teams of 15 Alliance and Horde players drop into a section of the Valley of the Four Winds from a pandaren Hot air balloon to race for food. Ingredients spawn across the map and appear on the minimap, and each must be picked up and delivered to their faction's cooking pot near Nomi. The first team to turn in 30 ingredients wins, but opposing players can ambush runners, steal ingredients, and sabotage deliveries to spice up the competition. Defeat the opposing faction's Virmen Thumper to gain their allegiance. Once defeated, it'll turn into a vehicle for a player to control and use abilities against the opposing faction.

The Coreway is an immense tunnel extending from Dornogal on the surface deep into Azeroth. It was built by the titan-forged so that the titans could study Azeroth's worldsoul without harming it. At one point, the Coreway extended all the way to the core of Azeroth; at present it terminates in the Ringing Deeps. The Coreway is found in the southwest corner of Dornogal. After fending off a nerubian invasion in They Come from Below, part of the Isle of Dorn storyline, the Coreway serves as the passage into the continent down to the Ringing Deeps. The Archive is on the western edge of its entrance, the Forgegrounds lie to the west, and a passage leads north to Keepers Terrace and Foundation Hall
The Core of O'ros is the remains of O'ros. It was never made available, but was perhaps planned to be retrieved after the naaru was destroyed during Bringer of the Light.

]] Cormaera are a species of flying, two-headed elemental predators that inhabited Azeroth during its earliest days and were subjugated by the Elemental Lords. They dominated the skies of Ragnaros' domain, and were often used as beasts of burden for his most loyal lieutenants during the elemental wars. In terms of both name and appearance, they resemble a mix of core hounds and chimaera.

Doing so will summon the Void-Forged Stallion, which drops the Void-Forged Stallion's Reins.

Daeyana Gleamgaard is an Arathi located in Wildcamp Or'lay in Azj-Kahet. She was gravely wounded, burned by nerubian poison, but the local haranir provided help to get better. When Hallowfall once again came under threat by the Sureki and the army was stretched thin, a call to arms was issued to those with the strength to wield a weapon. Daeyana answered the call, joining the Flame's Radiance. She was stationed at a camp to the south of the Untamed Valley in Azj-Kahet.

Daggerspine Point is an island on the western shore of Eversong Woods that has been claimed by the Daggerspine naga. It was formerly named Shalandis Isle. This area, including Daggerspine Landing, is one of the Ritual Sites.

The Cypher of the First Ones is the language of the enigmatic First Ones. It is not static like most other languages as it keeps evolving. The automa of Zereth Mortis speak the language of their creators in the form of a musical, runic language that is incomprehensible to mortal races. Despite his linguistic skills, the broker Firim found it a challenge to understand the cypher, which he realized was the key to understanding the First Ones' creations. Elder Eru has revealed that the automa's resistance to Domination magic stemmed from the language of the First Ones, phrases of which were buried in the Endless Sands.

Lireesa asked the rangers for their arrows and sent them back to the village. She managed to fire the arrows into the eagle, hitting its eyes, throat, and heart. Stepping into the areas marked by the Artillery Fire delve affix causes them to aim bombardments of arrows at the player. Completing a Tier 8 or higher Nightfall Sanctum run without triggering their Artillery Fire will award the Daystormer achievement.

Darkfuse Solutions (or Darkfuse Cartel) is a goblin cartel that has operated in numerous theatres across Azeroth and beyond. Originally known as the Blackfuse Company, it was led by the eponymous Siegecrafter Helix Blackfuse and provided advanced weaponry for the True Horde under the direct order of Warchief Garrosh Hellscream, such as the Iron Juggernaut. Their technology, most notably the Iron Star, paved the way for the weaponry used by the Iron Horde; whom they later also aligned with on . The company rebranded following the events of the war in Draenor, showing up again as Darkfuse Enforcement in Khaz Algar and Undermine as Jastor Gallywix's private army. Deepwind Dunk is a PvP Brawl where two teams of 15 Alliance and Horde players drop into Deepwind Gorge for a "basketball-style" resource race. Dunkballs spawn at three mines (center, north, and south) and must be carried back to the enemy base's basket either by sinking a long‐range shot or powering through for a dunk. Opponents can ambush carriers, steal balls, and swing momentum, and the team with the most scored baskets when time expires wins.
